title: blame, log -S and log -G
summary: Find who changed a line and why, and find the commit that added or removed any piece of code, even if the file was later deleted.

steps.title: blame: why is this line here?
body: Each line shows the **last commit that changed it**. The point is not *who to blame* but the commit: run `git show 9e8f7a6b` to read its message, the PR it came from, and the other lines it changed. That is why good messages matter.
| `-C` | follow lines moved or copied from other files |
| `--ignore-rev <id>` | skip a big reformatting commit (or list them in `.git-blame-ignore-revs`) |

steps.prompt: `git blame` says a buggy line was last changed in a commit titled *Run dotnet format on solution*. What is the most useful next step?
options: Re-run blame ignoring that commit (`--ignore-rev` or `-w`) to find the commit that really introduced the logic
Blame the person who ran the formatter
Give up: blame cannot see past it
steps.explain: Mechanical commits hide history. Teams list them in `.git-blame-ignore-revs` and set `blame.ignoreRevsFile` so everyone's blame skips them.

steps.title: The pickaxe: log -S and log -G
body: Blame only sees lines that still exist. To find when something **appeared or disappeared** anywhere in history:
git log -S "ApplyLegacyDiscount" --oneline       # commits that changed how many times the string occurs
git log -G "Retry\(\d+\)" --oneline             # commits whose diff has an added/removed line matching the regex
git log --follow -p -- src/Cart.cs               # one file's history, across renames
git grep "ApplyLegacyDiscount" v2.0              # search the code as it was in a tag
- `-S text` lists a commit only if the **number of occurrences** of `text` changed (it was added or removed). Moving it around within a file does not count.
- `-G regex` lists a commit if any added or removed line **matches**, even if the count is unchanged.

steps.prompt: `Cart.cs` evolved over four commits. Which commits does `git log -S "Legacy" --format=%h --reverse` list (oldest first, one per line)?
code: c3: moves  ApplyLegacy(); to another method  // still 1
steps.explain: The count went 0 -> 1 at c2 and 1 -> 0 at c4. c3 only moved the line, so the count stayed 1. `-G Legacy` would also have listed c3.

items: Who last changed line 42, and in which commit?
When was the call to `SendFax()` deleted?
Every change to `Cart.cs`, including before it was renamed from `Basket.cs`

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: find commits that added or removed the string `apiKey`, showing their diffs; then show who last changed lines 10 to 20, ignoring whitespace.
steps.explain: `-S` with `-p` is the fastest way to find when a secret, a flag or a function first appeared.

steps.title: Dig through history: -S, -L and blame -w
prompt: `~/shop/prices.sh` has a `discount()` function with a history. Answer three questions with Git, one answer file each:
1. `~/answers/removed.txt`: the subject of the commit that **removed** the call `applyLegacyDiscount`.
2. `~/answers/history.txt`: the subjects of every commit that changed the `discount()` function, newest first (one per line).
3. `~/answers/who.txt`: the name of the person who really wrote the line `local rate=15`. A bot re-indented the whole file since, so plain `git blame` points at the bot.

checks.name: removed.txt names the removing commit
checks.fail: `git log -S applyLegacyDiscount` lists the commits that changed how often the string appears: one added it, one removed it. Look at which is which with `-p`.

checks.name: history.txt follows discount()
checks.fail: `~/answers/history.txt` should list the commits that touched `discount()`. `git log -L :discount:prices.sh` follows one function.

checks.name: who.txt names the real author
checks.fail: Not the bot. `git blame -w` ignores whitespace-only changes and looks through the reformat.

hints: `git log -S applyLegacyDiscount --oneline -p` shows the two commits and their diffs: `+` added, `-` removed.
`git log -L :discount:prices.sh --format=%s -s` prints only the subjects (`-s` hides the diffs).
`git blame -w -L 3,3 prices.sh` shows the author of line 3 ignoring whitespace. `--ignore-rev <hash>` skips one commit by name.
steps.explain: The pickaxe (`-S`) finds when a string appeared or disappeared; `-G` matches any changed line against a regex. `log -L` follows a line range or a function through renames of the lines around it. For reformat commits, teams list them in a `.git-blame-ignore-revs` file and set `git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs`; GitHub's blame view reads the same file. `git blame -w -C -C` also follows code moved between files.
